subject: Commitment matrix and blackout exclusion proposal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightwave.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commitment matrix and blackout exclusion proposal

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I attached a version of the MSA redline that isolates the availability commitments into a single appendix (redline_msa_2027-09-28.docx) and a working uptime commitment matrix (uptime_commitment_matrix_v3.xlsx). Key changes called out for your team:

- We’re proposing a tiered uptime metric (99.9% / 99.95% / 99.99%) mapped to scaled credits so you can align spend to required availability.
- A narrow planned-maintenance blackout carveout for major infrastructure upgrades (windows will be scheduled in advance and limited to 2x per quarter; max 4 hours per event).
- An explicit emergency upgrade clause (customer-impacting but agreed maintenance to mitigate critical vulnerabilities) with a different credit calc.

Can you confirm BrightWave’s comfort with the blackout carveout size and the proposed calendar notification cadence (minimum 7 business days for standard maintenance)? If not, note which pieces you want us to loosen/tighten and we’ll reconcile with Legal.

If helpful, I can loop in Marissa and Kimberly from Legal for a short sync.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redline_msa_2027-09-28.docx (MS Word redline), uptime_commitment_matrix_v3.xlsx (Excel)

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightwave.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment matrix and blackout exclusion proposal

Sean —

Appreciate the docs and the clear framing. A couple of quick points from procurement & ops:

1) Blackout windows: BrightWave requires no more than 1x planned maintenance per quarter for core prod systems; 2x is a hard ask for our VP of Prod. Can you provide the rationale for 2x?
2) Notification cadence: 7 business days is doable for standard upgrades, but for rolling upgrades across regions we need per-region notices and an SLA that guarantees coordination with our change freeze periods (end of quarter).
3) Credits: can you show an example calculation for the 99.95% tier? The spreadsheet looks helpful but a worked example will speed approval.

I’m copying BrightWave Procurement (procurement@brightwave.com) — they’ll need a clean redline and a short cover note from Redwood summarizing the tradeoffs. We can do a 30-min call with your legal ops next week.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Cloud Ops — BrightWave

Sean / Kim —

Forwarding Lena's note. Quick internal take from Legal and Product:

- Blackout frequency: we can accept 1x planned maintenance per quarter if we narrow the definition of "core production" to exclude lower-tier non-critical clusters, and we tighten the maximum duration to 3 hours for those events.
- Notification: we should add a per-region notification clause and an explicit exception for change-freeze windows declared by the customer (they must publish freeze dates at least 15 days in advance).
- Credits calc: product suggests adding a worked example row in uptime_commitment_matrix_v3.xlsx and an appendix showing arithmetic for a monthly billing period.

Action items I propose:
1) Marcus to draft the 1-page cover note explaining tradeoffs (credits vs. maintenance frequency) for procurement.
2) Kim to prepare clean redline with our recommended tightening on duration and a per-region notification addendum.
3) Karthik to draft the worked example and confirm the math on emergency upgrade credit handling.

We should aim to have the materials back to BrightWave by Friday EOD so procurement can route internally.

Marissa

Marissa / team —

Attached is a short cover note draft (one page) that frames the tradeoffs for Procurement. Key bullets:

- Our proposed model reduces operational overhead and provides predictable credits scaled to impact.
- Limiting scheduled maintenance to 1x/quarter for core clusters is acceptable if maximum per-event window is 3 hours and per-region notices are included.
- Emergency upgrades remain subject to a different credit bucket; we propose a capped offset so customers are not left without remediation.

I also added two worked examples in the spreadsheet tab "Worked Examples": (a) 99.95% on a 30-day month => credit X; (b) 99.9% on a 30-day month => credit Y. Karthik, please confirm the calculations and emergency upgrade wording.

If everyone signs off I’ll finalize and send to Lena + procurement with Kim's clean redline.

Marcus
